baseline.label: baseline (the envelopes the swarm ran under)

caveats: The stream comes from simulated agents; real agents differ.
Replay is open-loop: agents do not react to refusals.
One envelope covers the whole stream and its daily budget is shared by every agent.
Leak includes bad orders that lie inside any envelope loose enough to let legitimate flow through.
The frontier is advice. The human reviews and signs; agents and the lab never choose or widen an envelope.

recommendation.explanation: On the recorded stream (about 4 simulated days), an envelope with a per-order cap of $91,360, a daily cap of $20,568,830, a 0.8% price band, 15 of 15 symbols on the allow-list and a human step-up above $66,976 and a fair-share limit of 0.5% of the daily cap per agent would have authorized $8,330,890/day of legitimate orders (95.9% of what honest agents proposed), refused 2.4% of legitimate proposals, leaked $219,347/day of bad orders (blocked 96.4% of bad notional) and asked a human to approve 42 orders/day. The envelopes the swarm actually ran under would have leaked $1,991,364/day with 6.1% false refusals and 58 approvals/day. Why this one: among candidates inside your risk budget it allows the most legitimate notional. What is left in the leak is bad orders that sit inside the envelope by design (an order at 95% of the cap is indistinguishable from a legitimate one); only a tighter envelope removes it, at the cost of the legitimate flow shown on the frontier. This is advice from a simulated stream; you review and sign. Agents never widen it.
